html: The Sisseton (Sisíthuŋwaŋ) are one of the four bands of the Eastern, or Santee, Dakota. In the 1700s and early 1800s they lived around the upper Minnesota River and the lakes on the border of present Minnesota and the Dakotas, such as Big Stone Lake and Lake Traverse, hunting bison and deer and trading furs. In the treaties of 1851 they sold most of their Minnesota land. After the Dakota War of 1862, in which many Sisseton took no part, the Dakota were driven out of Minnesota. In 1867 the Sisseton and Wahpeton received the Lake Traverse Reservation in north-eastern South Dakota, now the home of the Sisseton Wahpeton Oyate. To the west lived the Yanktonai.
